p.i: Respicit, & damnat sumpta infeliciter arma Proque tot insana quot credulitate triumphis Sperabat, numerat clades. Hunc diraphrenesis Abstulit, hunc maeror fugiendo dimicat ille, Et vicisse putat si visum effugerit hostem.

At columen generis, magni de femine Caroli, Ementitus annos, dulci qui plaudere somno Ipse sibi assuetus, voto complexus inani est Imperii ingentes incerto limite fines, Qui titulo Solymos, titulo Trinacria rura, Spe Gallos, spe Germanos, spe vate Britannos Spondebat, iacuit violata victima paci: Et scelere infestas, Polstroto vindice, terras Deseruit moriens, & spes finiuit auaras [?].

At tu qui nullo fortunae vulnere restas Lasus adhuc, cum germano impietate gemello, Carole, Romanique decus columenque senatus, Ne tibi concessum fortunae crede fauentis Munere, quod iusta nondum secuere securi Carnifices tibi colla manus: te feruat in orbis Ludibrium Nemesis: poena & graviore coercet, Quam si producto tetra de carceris umbra Funderet invisum populo plaudente cruorem, Aut coqueret lenta corpus feruore fauilla, Exemplo praedocta tuo. Mors terminus aui [?] est Omnibus ex aequo: nec poena, sed exitus, hinc ad Vitam aliam, solis nec tantum optabile iustis Perfugium, sed forte tibi. Nam tartara quamuis

page.notes: Long s rendered as s throughout. "infestas" read from the st ligature; "auaras" is doubtful (printed form looks like "anaras") and marked [?]. "aui" is doubtful and marked [?]. Verse lines are kept as printed with line breaks inside each stanza paragraph. The final "Inco-" stands alone at lower right and is the start of the next page's word, recorded as the catchword.
